title: Friction log and proposed patches — Mar 2026
body:
Purpose
-----
Quick synthesis of recurring customer friction and compiled feature asks from Q1–Q2 2026 conversations (support tickets, onboarding calls, account reviews). Intended for triage with product and platform engineering. This is a pragmatic, outcome-oriented log: for each friction we include frequency, representative customer quote, short-term patch, medium-term solution, rough effort (S/M/L), suggested owner, and next step.

Scope & method
--------------
Data sources: top 200 CS support threads since 2026-01-01; 12 onboarding kickoff calls; two executive QBRs; VOC survey (N=47). We grouped items by theme and de-duplicated via manual review. This is not exhaustive; it focuses on items that surfaced across >3 customers or where the ask is high-impact for revenue/retention.

Summary priority (quick view)
---------------------------
- High priority (ongoing churn / onboarding blockers): private deployment onboarding friction, billing/usage clarity for embeddings, SLA transparency for Dedicated.
- Medium priority (productive but causes frequent PM/eng touch): rollout/fallback visibility, streaming API quirks, KV-cache clearing behavior.
- Low priority (nice-to-have, low frequency): advanced batching controls in SDK, per-token quality scoring in console.

Detailed log (by theme)
-----------------------
1) Private deployment onboarding (highest frequency)
- Frequency: 16 distinct customers across finance, health, and legal sectors raised this in Q1.
- Representative quote: "Setting up VPC peering + KMS took three full days because the installer would silently retry on a few CNI errors; we couldn't get a deterministic runbook." — Platform lead, Azura Health
- Pain: unclear step failures, limited visibility into installer logs, manual ticket escalation required, contract/regulatory deadlines slipping.
- Short-term patch: add a guided installer mode with expanded (and persisted) log dump to S3/KMS after failures; short runbook checklist. (Effort: S)
- Medium-term solution: build an automated preflight checker that validates networking, KMS access, and GPU availability and outputs actionable remediation steps; integrate into onboarding portal. (Effort: M-L)
- Suggested owner: eng-private-deployments + solutions-engineering.
- Next step: schedule 1.5h sync with Solutions + Infra to draft preflight spec (owner: Maya). Create Jira: PLAT-785 (linked).

2) Billing and usage clarity for embeddings / batch inference
- Frequency: 12 customers + recurring CS questions. Enterprise and mid-market most affected.
- Representative quote: "Our analytics team can't reconcile embeddings cost with the token chart — are we charged per item or per byte after batching? This prevents approving Dedicated." — Revenue ops, Nimbus Analytics
- Pain: mismatch between console metrics, invoices, and SDK behavior; unclear cost model for batched embedding calls; refund/credit overhead for unexpected bills.
- Short-term patch: one-pager explaining billing for embeddings, examples (small, medium, large batch), and mapping to console metrics. Update invoices FAQ. (Effort: S)
- Medium-term solution: add a per-request cost breakdown UI for embeddings and batch endpoints (tokens, units billed, batch size), plus an exportable CSV for finance teams. (Effort: M)
- Suggested owner: product-hosted-api + finance.
- Next step: write draft one-pager and circulate to finance/legal for signoff (owner: Ravi). Create ticket: CS-4321.

3) Rollout/fallback visibility and deterministic behavior
- Frequency: 9 accounts (notably two large PLG customers).
- Representative quote: "We saw silent fallback to a cheaper variant during peak, but no audit trail — our SLOs alerted but we couldn't correlate to fallback events." — SRE, PixelForms
- Pain: lack of visibility in console/traces for routing decisions and fallbacks; debugging production incidents requires triage involving Redwood SRE.
- Short-term patch: add a rollout/fallback event stream to the request logs with structured tags (policy, source region, chosen model variant). Expose as a filterable view in the console. (Effort: M)
- Medium-term solution: enrich tracing/tracing-sampling with a rollout decision graph per request and an alerting rule templates pack for common fallback-induced regressions. (Effort: L)
- Suggested owner: console-and-rollouts + observability.
- Next step: prototype log enrichment (owner: Sofia). Link PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/987

4) Streaming API edge cases (client-level reconnection semantics)
- Frequency: 7 customers building live assistants/chat UIs.
- Representative quote: "When network blips happen, our frontend ends up with partial messages and we have to handle dedupe — would be great if the SDK gave clearer reconnection hooks." — Eng manager, Lapidot Labs
- Pain: inconsistent client experiences across SDKs, missing helper hooks for resuming streams vs restarting, partial message handling.
- Short-term patch: add documented best-practices snippet for reconnection + idempotency keys in SDK README and add a small helper in the JS SDK that wraps EventSource/WebSocket reconnection. (Effort: S)
- Medium-term solution: formalize a stream resume protocol (server-issued resume tokens + client SDK support) and server idempotency for partial responses. (Effort: L)
- Suggested owner: developer-experience + serving-runtime.
- Next step: open SDK task and add example app to developer-experience repo (owner: Ethan).

5) KV-cache and quantization surprise behavior
- Frequency: 5 customers and multiple internal E2E tests.
- Representative quote: "After we switched to the smaller quantized variant, answers got faster but occasionally truncated long-context leads — the cache behavior changed." — ML platform, Orion Retail
- Pain: behavior changes between variants (KV cache eviction, sequence length assumptions) creating unexpected regressions.
- Short-term patch: add a visible note in model-variant docs and in the console model catalog showing known KV/cache/seq-length tradeoffs. (Effort: S)
- Medium-term solution: expose explicit KV-cache configuration toggles (retention policy, prefix caching rules) per deployment and surface compatibility warnings on variant switch. (Effort: M)
- Suggested owner: serving-runtime + applied-ml.
- Next step: compile variant compat matrix and send to CS and docs for inclusion.

6) Dedicated capacity scaling and autoscale transparency
- Frequency: 8 accounts with Dedicated clusters.
- Representative quote: "Autoscale behaves like a black box — spikes are fine but our burst capacity costs are unpredictable." — Infra lead, Meridian Games
- Pain: unclear autoscale cooldown semantics, burst billing confusion, lack of per-route scaling metrics.
- Short-term patch: publish autoscale policy defaults and add per-route recent-scaling activity chart. (Effort: S)
- Medium-term solution: allow customers to configure explicit upper bounds for burst nodes and provide simulated cost previews for different scaling profiles. (Effort: M-L)
- Suggested owner: dedicated + observability.
- Next step: collect sample scaling graphs from three customers and add to product spec.

7) Console UX: route-level debugging and cost drilldowns
- Frequency: recurring ask in account reviews.
- Pain: console aggregates too much — customers want route -> model -> token cost mapping for recent requests, plus the ability to drill to single-request trace.
- Proposed patch: add a route-level view with top-N recent requests, latencies, and unit cost per request. (Effort: M)
- Owner: console-and-rollouts.
- Next step: wireframe session with PM and CS (Sofia).

Cross-cutting operational suggestions
----------------------------------
- Customer-facing playbook: compile a one-click troubleshooting checklist for top 5 onboarding failures (put in Confluence + link in support responses).
- Rapid rollback guardrails: standardize a fast-fallback runbook that solutions eng can execute for customers with contractual SLAs.
- Quarterly VOC digest: produce a 1-page signal snapshot for Eng/Prod with top 5 asks and suggested deadlines ahead of roadmap planning.

Open questions for triage
-------------------------
- Which of the medium-term items require infra/architectural approval (e.g., stream resume protocol, KV-cache toggles)? Need a brief impact doc.
- Are we willing to commit to bill/cost-preview features that expose near-real-time billing (legal/finance input needed on invoice alignment)?

Suggested prioritization rubric (for discussion)
------------------------------------------------
- Score = (CustomerImpact * Frequency * RevenueSignal) / EffortWeight
- Proposed cutoffs: 
  - Score > 50 -> prioritize this quarter
  - 25–50 -> next quarter
  - < 25 -> backlog
(We can run this against the items above in the triage meeting.)

Immediate next steps (owners & timeline)
---------------------------------------
- Draft embeddings billing one-pager and circulate to finance/legal (owner: Ravi) — due 2026-03-26.
- Preflight spec kickoff (owner: Maya) — meeting scheduled 2026-03-24.
- Console rollout event log prototype PR (owner: Sofia) — draft by 2026-04-02.
- SDK streaming helper snippet + example app (owner: Ethan) — prototype by 2026-03-30.

Appendix: representative ticket excerpts
---------------------------------------
- CS-12856: "Installer hangs on CNI apply, no logs dumped to console." — Azura Health.
- CS-12901: "Unexpected high embedding charges after switching to batch=50. Invoice mismatch." — Nimbus Analytics.
- CS-12944: "Fallback used during peak, model quality regressed — we need more info in the audit logs." — PixelForms.

Notes to self / rough TODOs
--------------------------
- Convert short-term patches into chores in Jira (list created above).
- Run prioritization rubric with product during roadmap slot on 2026-04-06.
- Share this doc with Solutions Eng leads and collect feedback in #cs-product-prioritization thread.

End of doc.
